title: SLO-aware cost allocator scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory scratchpad for an SLO-aware cost allocator that decides: when to route to spot vs on-demand vs reserved capacity, and which region/fallback tier to pick given a per-request latency SLO and cost objective. This is a notes-to-self style doc — rough sims, heuristics, and spreadsheet layout ideas.

TL;DR hypothesis:
- Significant unit cost savings (~15–35%) are available by making routing decisions per-request based on (1) measured cold/warm tail latency, (2) expected KV-cache/match to prefix (cache hit probability), and (3) bid/spot disruption risk.
- Savings only materialize if we (a) apply conservative SLO buffers for tail percentiles, and (b) maintain simple fallback chains (fast path -> reserved -> fallback region) to prevent SLA violations during spot preempts.

Assumptions used in sims (put these in spreadsheet columns):
- base_on_demand_cost_per_token_usd = 0.0000065
- spot_discount = 0.65 (i.e., spot is 35% of on-demand cost) — variable across regions
- reserved_effective_cost = 0.8 * on_demand (amortized committed capacity)
- avg_tokens_per_request = 60 (explore 20/60/200 buckets)
- p_cache_hit = 0.25 (probability KV/prefix already warm; strongly workload-dependent)
- cold_start_penalty_ms = 120 (extra latency if model not warmed in chosen pool)
- network_delta_ms(region) = {local: 6, cross-region: 26} (use spreadsheet per-region values)
- SLO = 150ms p95 (configurable per-customer/route)
- acceptable_cost_increase_for_stability = +10% (max relative cost vs baseline to reduce errors)

Key metrics we need per-route in sheet (columns):
- route_id, avg_qps, avg_tokens, p95_latency_observed_hosted, cache_hit_rate_est, region_latency_ms, spot_availability_score (0..1), on_demand_cost_per_token, spot_cost_per_token, reserved_cost_per_token, fallback_chain (ordered list as string), expected_cost_per_request, expected_p95_latency, risk_score (composite)

Quick scenario sketches (hand calculations in scratchpad):
1) High QPS, high cache (p_cache_hit=0.6):
- Warm path to spot in local region preferred, because cache hits reduce compute; fallback reserved local if spot preempted.
- Expected per-request cost: tokens*spot_cost ~ 60 * 0.0000065 * 0.35 = $0.00001365 per request (very rough).
- Latency budget: warm path p95 ~ 60ms (well below SLO). We can be aggressive with spot usage.

2) Low QPS, cold-sensitive (cache_hit=0.05, bursts):
- Spot risky: cold_start_penalty + network delta if routed cross-region might blow p95. Prefer reserved or on-demand in local reserved pool and allow occasional cross-region fallback for overloads.
- If cold_start adds 120ms, p95 likely > SLO; must route to warm pool. Cost increase acceptable.

3) Multi-region mix with price arbitrage:
- If spot in us-west is 40% cheaper than local reserved but network + tail risks add 30ms -> for SLO=120ms p95, we can route only requests with expected warm-hit probability > X (solve from spreadsheet).

Heuristic decision rules (starter):
- If expected_p95_latency(routed_to_spot_local) <= SLO - safety_margin_ms AND spot_availability_score >= 0.7 => route to spot_local.
- Else if reserved_local has capacity and expected_cost <= on_demand*0.95 => route reserved_local.
- Else if cross-region_on_demand expected_p95 <= SLO and cost delta < acceptable_cost_increase => route cross-region_on_demand.
- Else: failover to host-tier with best historical p95 (could be higher cost but preserves SLO).

Safety margins to compute:
- safety_margin_ms = max(0.1 * SLO, 25ms)
- when cache_hit_prob unknown, assume conservative 0.15 for decisioning; post-facto adapt with decaying EWMA per-route.

Spreadsheet layout idea (tabs):
- params: global constants, region prices, historic spot preempt rates
- routes: per-route traffic attributes (qps, tokens_dist, historical cache_hit, p95_baseline)
- sim_engine: per-row scenario with chosen routing policy, returns expected_cost and expected_p95 (vector formulas)
- experiments: Monte Carlo sweeps over spot_availability (0.3..0.99), cache_hit (0..0.9), cold_penalty (60..300ms)
- rollout_plan: mapping of policies to canary buckets (e.g., start with 1% of traffic where predicted savings > 25% and predicted risk_score < 0.2)

Monte Carlo notes (rough):
- For each sim sample: sample spot_up ~ Bernoulli(spot_availability_score), sample cache_hit ~ Bernoulli(cache_hit_prob), sample cold_penalty ~ Normal(mean, sigma). Compute latency = base_model_latency * (1 - cache_hit) + cold_penalty*(1-cached_warm) + network_delta. Track whether > SLO. Cost = tokens * cost_per_token(selected_pool) + warmup_cost_if_any.
- Output: expected_cost, percent_samples_breaching_SLO, expected_extra_tokens_wasted (due to retries/fallbacks).

Actionable recommendations (for next week sprint):
- Build the sim spreadsheet with the five tabs above and populate with a) 10 representative routes (high qps, steady; bursty; low qps; long-context; embedding-heavy) and b) region price examples (us-east/us-west/eu). Owner: me + Dmitri.
- Implement small server-side policy shim: takes route metadata and returns prioritized candidate pools (spot_local, reserved_local, on_demand_local, cross_region_on_demand) with estimated cost and p95. Keep policy deterministic and log decisions. (PR tracked in linked_artifacts).
- Run A/B canary: start with 1% of traffic for routes where predicted savings >= 20% and predicted p95_violation_prob < 1%. Gradually expand to 10% after 48h if observed violations < threshold.
- Metric hooks: p95 by policy, retry rate, fallback frequency, mean cost per request, savings realized vs baseline.

Open questions / caveats:
- How to get accurate per-request cache hit estimate? We can approximate from recent prefix/KV stats but per-request classifier might be better (but costs extra compute).
- Spot availability modeling: internal signals (spot termination notices) exist, but we need historical per-region signal -> convert to daily availability scores. Who owns that dataset? (cc: Marcus)
- Pricing churn: spot/on-demand delta can change quickly. We need daily refresh and a throttled policy for re-evaluating route-level decisions.

Quick TODOs (short):
- [ ] Build spreadsheet skeleton (params, routes, sim_engine) — Claire (2d)
- [ ] Pull region price snapshot + historical spot preempt table — Marcus (3d)
- [ ] Add telemetry hooks to policy shim prototype — Dmitri (1w)
- [ ] Draft canary rollout doc + SLO guardrails — Claire (3d)

Notes to self: keep the policy simple at first. Overfitting per-request features in the policy increases risk. Start with conservative thresholds and a short feedback loop (48–72h) to adjust heuristics.

References & links (inlined):
- spreadsheet skeleton: sheets/new?copy=optimize-sim-template (placeholder)
- related: confluence:OPT-452-slo-routing-design, Github PR linked above.

End of scratchpad.
